title: Montezuma Cypress: Ancient Ahuehuetes You Can Visit
meta_description: Mexico's ahuehuete. El Árbol del Tule in Oaxaca, one tree by DNA, has the stoutest trunk on earth, 42 metres round by a 2005 laser survey.
intro: Taxodium mucronatum is Mexico's national tree, the ahuehuete, planted at springs by the Aztecs, and it holds the stoutest trunk on earth. El Árbol del Tule, in a church courtyard in Oaxaca, measured 42 metres round in a 2005 laser survey; its trunk is so lobed that botanists long assumed it was several trees fused together until DNA work in the 1990s showed it is one. Its age is put at 1,400 to 1,600 years on growth-rate grounds. Mexico City began protecting its ahuehuetes by name in 2025: El Sabino de San Juan is 18.5 metres round. In Europe, Florence's is seven metres around and was hit by lightning barely a decade ago, Naples has nicknamed its own the Tree of Thule, and Madrid's in the Retiro's parterre comes with two origin stories that cannot both be true.
